newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close slightly higher in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close slightly higher in thin trade.

text.p: Italian shares closed mostly higher on Tuesday, helped by remarks in the afternoon by Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini that talks with European partners on a return of the lira to the European exchange rate mechanism were going well.

Trading volumes were well up on Monday's levels, which had been depressed by the lack of overseas orders resulting from the market holiday in London, but were still low at 315 billion lire. The market was still casting around for a clear direction.
The all-share mibtel index finished 0.5 percent higher at 9,649 while the blue chip mib30 ended 0.63 percent up.
Brokers said today's recovery followed a sell-off yesterday prompted by the latest government controversy over membership of European and monetary union.
"A lot of uncertainties in the coming weeks have been discounted," said a Milan-based equities salesman. "Most people are underweight to neutral at the moment."
Shares in television group Mediaset recovered strongly after the government signalled a decree law would be passed extending television franchises.
The prospect of a legal vacuum after a deadline for new broadcasting legislation runs out on Tuesday night had prompted fears that one of Mediaset's channels might be forced off the air.

Mediaset closed 1.7 percent higher at 7,127 lire. Eni finished fractionally easier, Fiat was 0.57 percent firmer at 4,733 lire. Telecom stocks ended firmer, led by Stet, up 1.83 percent at the close to 4,889 lire.
